biggest_catch: UserTesting publishes no official general payout — every amount is per-test on your dashboard, so the concrete-payout requirement fails on official terms alone; payments also land ~14 days after each test.
catches: No official published pay range; each test's pay is shown only on your dashboard before you accept.
Payments arrive usually 14 days after test completion — days, not today.
A verified PayPal account in good standing is required to receive anything.
The practice test in the application is unpaid.
Customers can request refunds; the Quality Team reviews and can cancel a payment.

c1.evidence: Official UserTesting Contributor Support Center describes the contributor program and payment process.

c2.evidence: No concrete payout in official terms: 'Payment amounts vary based on the test type, duration, and customer demand — your dashboard will always show you the amount you'll get paid for each test.'

c3.evidence: Official FAQ: 'We send your test payment to your linked PayPal account, usually 14 days after you complete a test.'

c4.evidence: No participation fee in official materials; the practice test is unpaid but free to take.

eligibility: Complete the applicant checklist (confirm email, link verified PayPal, complete profile, pass practice test); tests matched to your profile
maximize: Not verifiable as a route — UserTesting publishes no general pay range. Only accept tests whose dashboard-listed pay you would accept; every test shows its amount before you accept.
notes: Official timing fits a 'days' cadence (usually 14 days via PayPal), but without an official published payout range or test duration this cannot be a verified route. Third-party pay claims ($10–$60+) were excluded.
